text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri chairs an expanded ministerial meeting today and tomorrow, bringing together 14 ministers, 33 businessmen and many others, to follow up implementation of the deals made at the Middle East economic conference in Cairo last week.

- President Hosni Mubarak flew home from Abu Dhabi yesterday after a successful summit meeting with Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan. Informed sources in the United Arab Emirates said Mubarak wanted to tell Sheikh Zaid that he named the Western desert canal after him because of his support for Egypt.

- Local Government Minister Mahmoud Sherif said the ministry had taken immediate measures to face the danger of floods, including setting up an operations room which operates around the clock to follow the situation and contact officials if any disaster happens.

- Gamal Mubarak, a member of the U.S.-Egyptian presidents council and son of the president, said the government was preparing a new bill to give investors more advantages, along the lines followed in developed countries, as recommended by the Cairo economic conference.
- The level of the water behind the High Dam rose three cms (more than one inch) yesterday to reach 178.55 metres, the highest level since the dam was built.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said that Egypt is making contacts on Egyptian participation in the proposed U.N. peacekeeping force for Zaire.
- Ganzouri will hold a meeting today of the ministerial group on the Toshka project.
- Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali said the success of the Cairo economic conference would help towards desert reclamation plans and increasing agricultural exports.

- The three-month period set by the United Nations for Sudan to hand over those accused of trying to assassinate Mubarak ran out yesterday. The U.N. Security Council will start consultations on what to do next.

- At the end of this week the state security prosecutor will announce the results of the questioning of Israeli Azam Azam and Egyptian Emad Abdelhalim Ismail, both suspected of spying for Israel. They will then be referred to the supreme state security court for trial.

- President Mubarak is giving priority at this stage to giant development projects. Within days he will open the third tunnel in the Peace Canal project to irrigate 400,000 acres (160,000 hectares) in Sinai and 220,000 acres (90,000) west of the Suez Canal.
- The national census starts on Tuesday. More than 100,000 census takers are taking part.
- Floods brought traffic to a standstill in the Red Sea resort of Hurghada and along the main road to Cairo. In Sohag province 16 houses fell down because of the floods.
